claims.quote: In some of these failures, the agent considers an implementation choice that meets a requirement, but later decides to commit to another one that does not meet the requirement for a reason it finds acceptable. We call this specification satisficing.

claims.what: why it is hard; self-correction bias
claims.quote: It is challenging to identify and mitigate specification satisficing because the agent accepts such choices for its own reasons, and existing self-correction methods are biased toward them.
We propose SatisFix, which guides a coding agent to report these choices and their reasons, and then check each choice against the task description.
We evaluate SatisFix on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Pro with five LLMs as backbones and two different agent frameworks, and compare it with three self-correction methods.

claims.what: pass@1 lift over the base agent
claims.quote: SatisFix improves the pass@1 of the base agent by an average of 5.09% on DeepSWE and 7.06% on the hard subset of SWE-bench Pro.
On DeepSWE, it outperforms the best baseline by 3.98%.
claims.metric: pass@1 margin over best self-correction baseline

claims.quote: Our ablation study shows that both steps of SatisFix contribute to the improvement.
